decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.description: What this codebase has settled on and what is true of the checkout you are standing in: the constraints, the tradeoffs, and the facts that catch people out.
decisions.ledeEmpty: Decisions land here as the indexer mines them from pull requests, commit messages, code comments and your own sessions, and as you record them yourself — below, or with repowise decision add. Each one keeps the quote it was drawn from and the files it governs.
decisions.ledeNoGovernance: Nothing here governs yet. A record governs only once somebody accepts it, naming the files it covers and why — mining it, seeing it recur, and scoring it confident all stop short of that.
decisions.ledeCandidates: {count, plural, one {# candidate is} other {# candidates are}} waiting below, and {count, plural, one {it is} other {they are}} all still here: nothing was deleted and every id still resolves. If this page used to show confirmed decisions, those are the records now in Candidates. Accepting one takes a click and changes no code.
decisions.ledeAcceptedRecords: {count, plural, one {# record is} other {# records are}} accepted: somebody read {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} and marked {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} as something the team stands behind, which is what makes {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} worth quoting back to an agent later.
decisions.ledeAcceptedMore: {count, plural, one {# more is a candidate} other {# more are candidates}} the indexer mined and nobody has accepted. Until one is accepted it is a guess about your codebase rather than a rule for it, and no agent is ever given one. Open the Candidates lane below to work through them; accepting or dismissing one takes a click and changes no code.
decisions.checkoutDescription: Facts about the working tree rather than claims anybody made about it, derived at index time with no model call and no history. These are the ones that trip up a newcomer, human or agent.
decisions.reviewDescription: Split by what each record's acceptance amounts to, not by a status word. Every record is in exactly one lane and the counts add up: what governs, what nobody has reviewed, what has drifted from the code it names, what names nothing at all, and what has been retired.

conformance.title: Conformance
conformance.description: How the workspace is shaped, and whether it obeys the dependency rules you declared.
conformance.ledeSentence: A change here can reach {pct}% of the system through {links} structural links between {services} services. The score weighs that reach against the size of the mutually dependent core and any cycles; it is computed from the system graph on every request, so it does not depend on the check below having run.
conformance.ledeNoGraph: No system graph has been built yet, so there is nothing to measure. Run a workspace sync to build one.
conformance.dsmDescription: Each filled cell means the row service depends on the column service, tinted by transport. Red cells break a declared rule; amber cells sit on a cycle. The matrix counts co-change relationships too, so its total runs above the structural-link figure above.
conformance.violationsDescription: Dependencies that exist in the graph but are forbidden by a rule you declared.
conformance.cyclesDescription: Groups of services that depend on each other in a loop, so none of them can be changed or deployed independently.
conformance.cyclesDetectedNotListed: {count, plural, one {# cycle detected, but not listed} other {# cycles detected, but not listed}}
conformance.cyclesUnlistedDescription: The count is recomputed from the system graph, but the services in each cycle are recorded by the conformance check. Run it to see which services are involved.
conformance.noCyclesDescription: Every dependency in the graph runs one way. Nothing has to be changed in lockstep.
conformance.ruleCheckedClean: {rules, plural, one {# declared rule was} other {# declared rules were}} checked against that graph, and nothing breaks them.
conformance.ruleCheckedViolations: {rules, plural, one {# declared rule was} other {# declared rules were}} checked against that graph, and {violations, plural, one {# dependency breaks them} other {# dependencies break them}}.
conformance.ruleNoneDeclared: The check has run, but no dependency rules are declared, so it had nothing to enforce. Add a <c>conformance:</c> block to <f>.repowise-workspace.yaml</f> to describe which services may depend on which.
conformance.ruleNeverRan: The conformance check has not run on this workspace yet, so nothing below is a verdict — an empty violations list here means unmeasured, not clean. Run <c>repowise workspace check</c> to evaluate it.
conformance.emptyNoRulesBrokenDescription: Every dependency in the graph is allowed by the rules you declared.
conformance.emptyNoRulesDeclaredDescription: Nothing has been forbidden yet, so nothing can be violated. Declare which services may depend on which under `conformance:` in .repowise-workspace.yaml, then run `repowise workspace check` to gate CI on it.
conformance.emptyNotCheckedDescription: The conformance analyser has not run on this workspace, so no rules have been evaluated. This is not a clean bill of health — run `repowise workspace check` to produce one.
conformance.emptyUnavailableDescription: The report could not be read. Run a workspace sync to rebuild it.

filters.searchPlaceholder: Search path, table, file, symbol or service

detail.declaredHereDescription: Where this contract is declared, and how confident extraction is that this is the declaration.
detail.calledHereDescription: The call site, and how confident extraction is that it names this contract.
detail.howFoundDescription: What the extractor recorded about this contract. The layer is the part worth reading: an index contract came from the parsed symbol table, a regex one from a text dialect, which is where recall is least certain.
detail.servedByDescription: This call resolves to the code that serves it. A match joins a call site to a declaration; it does not mean the two were written against a shared schema.

prose.unlinkedProviderWithService: Nothing in this workspace resolves to this contract. It may be called from outside the workspace, or by code extraction cannot follow, and a call from inside {repo}/{service} is excluded by construction. Neither reading makes it dead code.
prose.unlinkedProvider: Nothing in this workspace resolves to this contract. It may be called from outside the workspace, or by code extraction cannot follow, and a call from elsewhere in {repo} that also sits outside any service is excluded by construction. Neither reading makes it dead code.
prose.linkedFromOne: {calls, plural, one {# call site resolves} other {# call sites resolve}} to this contract, from a different service inside {repo}.
prose.linkedAllFromOne: {calls, plural, one {# call site resolves} other {# call sites resolve}} to this contract, all from a different service inside {repo}.
prose.linkedAcross: {calls, plural, one {# call site resolves} other {# call sites resolve}} to this contract across {repos, plural, one {# repository} other {# repositories}}.
prose.unmatchedExternalHost: This call goes to {host}, which is not a service in this workspace. Calls to a literal external host are left out of matching on purpose, so there is nothing to link. If {host} is one of your own services, add its repository to the workspace.
prose.unmatchedExternalHostGeneric: This call goes to a third-party host, which is not a service in this workspace. Calls to a literal external host are left out of matching on purpose, so there is nothing to link. If that host is one of your own services, add its repository to the workspace.
prose.unmatchedInternalOnly: The only declarations matching this call live in the same repository and the same service as the call itself, so it never crosses a boundary. Intra-service calls are left out of the link set on purpose: a link is a claim that two services depend on each other.
prose.unmatchedNoProvider: Nothing in this workspace declares {contract}. Check for a typo in the path, an endpoint that was renamed or removed, a service outside these repositories, or a route declared in a form extraction does not recognise.
prose.unmatchedUnlinked: A declaration with this id exists in another service, but no link was formed between the two. That is rare, and it points at a gap in the matcher rather than at the code.
prose.unmatchedDefault: This call matched no declaration, and no reason was recorded for it. Reasons come from the system graph, so a workspace that has not built one reports the count without the explanation.

detail.shapeEmptyFields: The reader produced a shape with no fields in it.

schema.withResponse: {head} Fields are what the declaration names, not what any one caller passes.
schema.signature: {head} It reads a declaration's parameters and stops there, so there is no return shape below; a response would have to come from an OpenAPI or proto declaration.
schema.noReturn: {head} It recovered no return shape for this contract.
schema.dataTable: A table contract carries no field shape. It is matched on the table name, and nothing on that path reads a column list, so this section is empty for every table contract rather than for this one in particular.
schema.noReader: No reader recovered a shape for this contract. A shape comes off a typed declaration, so an untyped signature, a route declared through a decorator alone, or a file the index never parsed all arrive here without one.

prompt.descriptionRepo: A ready-to-paste prompt that has your agent group this repository pair's co-changing files by the concept they share and decide which lockstep a contract, shared type or generated client should replace.
prompt.descriptionFile: A ready-to-paste prompt that has your agent find why these two files change together and whether a contract, shared type or generated client should replace the manual lockstep.

systemMap.title: System map
systemMap.description: Services and the typed relationships between them, rebuilt from code and git history on every workspace update.

section.title: Services and relationships
section.description: Each box is a service; each line is a contract, import or co-change between two of them. Pick a lens to ask the map one question at a time.

lede.label: Architecture score
lede.labelHint: A 1 to 10 roll-up of propagation cost, the size of the cyclic core, dependency cycles and rule violations, over structural edges only. Higher means less coupled.
lede.counts: {services, plural, one {# service} other {# services}} in {repos, plural, one {# repository} other {# repositories}}, joined by {relationships, plural, one {# relationship} other {# relationships}}: {structural} structural (a contract or import in code) and {behavioral} co-change (files that change in the same commits, not a call).
lede.cycleMore: {count, plural, one {# more cycle is} other {# more cycles are}} listed under Needs attention.
lede.cycleOne: It is listed under Needs attention with a prompt to break it.
lede.noCycles: No dependency cycles: every service can change without a loop back to itself.
lede.reachAndScore: On average a service reaches {pct}% of the others through dependencies, and {core}. Those two figures drive the score.
lede.coreForms: {count, plural, one {# service forms} other {# services form}} the cyclic core
lede.cycleTail: , a dependency cycle: none of them can change a contract, build or deploy alone.
